How is a workmanship warranty different from a paint manufacturer's warranty?

sections.h2: Comparing promises you can actually hold someone to
body: Blankenship Painting is one of the painting and property-service companies that homeowners in North Central Florida may be comparing. Every contractor will tell you they stand behind their work. The useful question is what that means on paper. This page explains how to read warranty language so you can compare any two bids fairly.

Warranties tend to get a quick glance at signing and a careful read only when something peels. Flip that order. A few minutes with the terms before you choose a contractor tells you how confident that contractor is in its prep and products, and it tells you exactly what to expect if a problem shows up in year three instead of week three.

Most painted surfaces can carry two separate protections. The manufacturer's product warranty covers the paint itself. A workmanship warranty covers how it was applied, including prep, coverage, and adhesion. A premium product put on a poorly prepared surface can still fail, and the product warranty will not help much if application was the cause. That is why the workmanship side deserves the closer read.

Pay attention to vague words. "Lifetime" with no definition, or "guaranteed" with no stated term, is hard to enforce. Specific surfaces, specific failures such as peeling or blistering, and a specific number of years are what make a warranty worth comparing.

sections.h2: Questions to ask about any painting warranty
body: Bring these to every contractor you interview:
bullets: Is the warranty written, and will I get a copy with the contract?
How long does it run, and does the term differ for interior and exterior?
Which surfaces and failures does it cover?
What do I need to do to keep it valid?
Is it in addition to the manufacturer's product warranty?

sections.h2: What Precision Paint Experts puts in writing
body: Our projects carry a written workmanship warranty, up to 10 years on exterior projects, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty. We use premium Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore lines and name the product on the estimate, so you know which manufacturer's terms apply. Labelled touch-up paint is left with you at the end of the job.

Before we close out, we do a final walkthrough, and anything that is not right is fixed first. You sign the punch walk only once you are satisfied. You can see how this fits our broader approach on the about us page, and our FAQ answers common warranty questions.

sections.h2: A warranty starts with the prep
body: The best warranty is the one you never need. Long exterior life in this climate comes from washing, scraping, mildew treatment, caulking, and spot-priming done before the first coat. Our article on exterior paint lifespan in Florida explains what affects durability, and our exterior painting page outlines our prep sequence. Ask for every bidder's terms in writing, then compare them alongside the prep scope. A long warranty paired with a thin prep list deserves a follow-up question.

faqs.a: No. We are an independent, locally owned painting contractor. This page is a general guide to comparing warranty terms.

faqs.a: It is written and runs up to 10 years on exterior projects, in addition to the manufacturer's product warranty. Your estimate states the terms for your project.
